title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles Leiserson, Ronald Rivest, Clifford Stein
description: Comprehensive textbook on algorithm design and analysis: sorting, graphs, dynamic programming, greedy methods and complexity.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms in Python
author: Michael T. Goodrich, Roberto Tamassia, Michael H. Goldwasser
description: Data structures such as stacks, queues, trees, hash tables and graphs, implemented and analysed in Python.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A handbook of writing readable, maintainable code with practical rules for naming, functions and refactoring.

title: Software Engineering
author: Ian Sommerville
description: Covers the software process, requirements, design, testing and project management.

title: Python Crash Course
author: Eric Matthes
description: Hands-on introduction to Python programming for beginners, with projects including a game, a data visualisation and a web app.

title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
author: Al Sweigart
description: Beginner-friendly guide to using Python to automate everyday tasks such as files, spreadsheets and web scraping.

title: Learning Python
author: Mark Lutz
description: In-depth tutorial on the Python language, its types, functions, classes and modules.

title: The C Programming Language
author: Brian W. Kernighan, Dennis M. Ritchie
description: The classic introduction to the C language by its creators.

title: Let Us C
author: Yashavant Kanetkar
description: Beginner-oriented introduction to C programming with many solved examples.

title: Eloquent JavaScript
author: Marijn Haverbeke
description: Modern introduction to JavaScript, programming concepts and browser programming.

title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras and TensorFlow
author: Aurelien Geron
description: Practical introduction to machine learning and deep learning with scikit-learn, Keras and TensorFlow.

title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
author: Christopher M. Bishop
description: Rigorous textbook on probabilistic machine learning, classification, regression and graphical models.

title: Deep Learning
author: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville
description: Textbook covering neural networks, optimisation and modern deep learning methods.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
author: Stuart Russell, Peter Norvig
description: Leading textbook on artificial intelligence: search, knowledge, reasoning, planning and learning.

title: Introduction to Information Retrieval
author: Christopher D. Manning, Prabhakar Raghavan, Hinrich Schutze
description: Covers search engines, TF-IDF, vector space models, indexing and text classification.

title: Python for Data Analysis
author: Wes McKinney
description: Data wrangling and analysis in Python using pandas, NumPy and Jupyter.

title: Database System Concepts
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth, S. Sudarshan
description: Core database textbook: relational model, SQL, normalisation, transactions and storage.

title: Fundamentals of Database Systems
author: Ramez Elmasri, Shamkant B. Navathe
description: Introduction to database design, ER modelling, SQL and database internals.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: How to build reliable, scalable systems: storage, replication, partitioning and stream processing.

title: Computer Networks
author: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, David J. Wetherall
description: Introduction to computer networks, protocols, the internet, TCP/IP and network security.

title: Operating System Concepts
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin, Greg Gagne
description: Processes, threads, scheduling, memory management, file systems and security in operating systems.

title: Introduction to the Theory of Computation
author: Michael Sipser
description: Automata, formal languages, computability and complexity theory.

title: Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
author: Kenneth H. Rosen
description: Logic, sets, combinatorics, graph theory and proofs for computer science students.
